h1: Graduate visa cut to 18 months: apply before 31 December 2026
title: Graduate Visa Cut to 18 Months: Apply Before 2027 | UVS
description: The Graduate visa drops from 2 years to 18 months from 1 January 2027. Find out who is affected and why you should apply before 31 December 2026.
intro: From 1 January 2027, the UK Graduate visa will be granted for 18 months instead of 2 years for most graduates. If you have finished, or are about to finish, a degree in the UK, applying before the end of 2026 could give you six extra months to work.

sections.heading: What is changing?
sections.text:
The Graduate visa lets international students stay and work in the UK after completing a degree, without needing an employer to sponsor them. Applications made on or before 31 December 2026 are granted 2 years. Applications made on or after 1 January 2027 will be granted 18 months for bachelor's and master's graduates.

PhD and other doctoral graduates will still be granted 3 years.

sections.heading: Who can apply now?
sections.text:
You can usually apply for the Graduate visa if:
- You are in the UK on a Student visa
- You have successfully completed your course
- Your university has reported your completion to the Home Office
- Your Student visa hasn't expired

What matters is the date the Home Office receives your application, not the date of your graduation ceremony.

sections.heading: What should you do?
sections.text:
If your university has already confirmed your completion, apply as soon as possible, and before 31 December 2026 if you can. If you're waiting for results, keep in touch with your university about when it will report your completion, and have your documents ready.

The application fee is £937, plus the Immigration Health Surcharge of £1,035 for each year of the visa.

sections.heading: After the Graduate visa
sections.text: The Graduate visa can't be extended and doesn't lead directly to settlement. Many graduates use it to gain experience and then switch to a Skilled Worker visa with an employer, where lower "new entrant" salary thresholds may apply.

faqs.q: Can I still get a 2-year Graduate visa?
faqs.a: Yes, if the Home Office receives your application on or before 31 December 2026 and you meet the requirements.

faqs.q: Does the change affect PhD graduates?
faqs.a: No. PhD and other doctoral graduates will still be granted 3 years.
